title.narrative: PPDP 2.0 - MSD for Inclusive Decent Employment and Productive Livelihoods
PPDP 2.0 - MSD for Inclusive Decent Employment and Productive Livelihoods

description.narrative: Insatsen är en fortsättning på stödet till Inclusive Economic Growth through Decent Work in the Great Rift Valley (insats nr 10305). Den är en sk Public Private Development Partnership som genomförs av ILO i samarbete med ForumCiv samt privata och offentliga aktörer i Narok, Nakuru och Kajiado län. Insatsen syftar till att skapa förutsättningar för ökade och förbättrade arbets- och försörjningsmöjligheter med anständiga arbetsvillkor. Stort fokus ska läggas på den gröna omställningen, jämställdhet och SRHR. Erfarenheter, lärdomar och best practices från första fasen ska skalas upp genom att stödet antar en Market Systems Development-ansats.

The contribution is a continuation of the PPDP for Inclusive Economic Growth through Decent Work in the Great Rift Valley (contribution no 10305). This PPDP 2.0 will be implemented by ILO in close collaboration with ForumCiv and together with public and private actors in Narok, Nakuru and Kajiado counties. It aims at increased job creation and improved conditions for job opportunities, self employment and livelihoods. Great focus will be given to the green transition, gender equality and SRHR. Experiences, lessons learned and best practices from the first phase will be scaled up by applying a Market Systems Development (MSD) Approach to the project implementation.

The overarching aim of the project is to contribute to the inclusive and sustainable socio-economic development in the Great Rift Valley, with the overall development objective being to promote the creation of inclusive productive employment and livelihoods.
To contribute to these overall objectives, the specific objectives for the programme are the following outcomes:
- enhanced employability and job access through vocational education and skills development;
- growing sustainable enterprises and value chains for increased inclusive job opportunities; and
- improved opportunities for inclusive and productive employment and sustainable livelihoods at community level through enhanced community engagement.

title.narrative: PPDP 2.0 ­ MSD FOR INCLUSIVE DECENT EMPLOYMENT AND PRODUCTIVE LIVELIHOODS

description.narrative:
The reporting period mainly constituted a transition phase from the project's first phase (pure PPDP) to its current second phase, in which the PPDP partnership model has adopted a Market Systems Development (MSD) approach. During the period (July 2024 - December 2025), the project has consolidated the technical, institutional, and analytical groundwork, which provides the foundation required to operationalise a comprehensive MSD approach in the tourism and fodder sectors. Implementation of project activities started towards the end of 2025.
Most planned outputs for both the transition phase and project implementation were delivered as planned. Examples of achievements and output results include:
Transition (to MSD approach) implementation:
• Over 150 stakeholders trained on MSD principles.
• Rapid Market Assessments and Market Systems Analyses for fodder and tourism sectors completed, providing a strong evidence base for systemic intervention design.
• Based on the MSAs, a portfolio of 10 MSD interventions (5 per sector) was designed through participatory cocreation; 5 priority models selected for roll-out in 2026.
• Nakuru County institutionalised a Tourism Department, with dedicated budget allocations a major system change, and a full staff complement led by a Director of Tourism.
• Policy and regulatory progress: Three county bills under development to regulate hay and silage trade, strengthen quality assurance, and formalize markets.
• The Gender Action Plan (GAP) was completed, which is guiding the project engagement with county governments and private sector partners
Project implementation:
Outcome 1 - Skills development and Employment
• Skills gaps analyses in Nakuru, Narok and Kajiado counties were carried out to align skills development with labor market demands in tourism and fodder sectors for sustainability.
• Mapping of Work Based Learning (WBL) ecosystems in all three counties was carried out, providing the groundwork for a National Quality Apprenticeship Framework - scheduled for implementation in 2026.
Outcome 2: Enterprise Development in Fodder and Tourism
• Adoption of quality standards: Kenya Bureau of Standards (KEBS) and counties fully financed standards clinics for fodder and silage markets.
• Access to Finance: Engagement with KCB, Equity Bank, and AFC to develop tailored financial products matching tourism seasonality and fodder cash flow.
Outcome 3 - Community Engagement and Inclusion
• Project integrated Rights-Based Approaches to embed inclusion, accountability, and participation by engaging local associations and employers to participate in county level tourism and fodder sector coordination platforms.
• Endorsement by the Kenya cabinet on Care economy policy to which the project highly offered both technical and financial support during its drafting.
Outcome A: Sustainability of the multi-stakeholder partnership
• Partner contributions - from public, private and social partners - increased from 15% of Sidas allocation in 2024 to 35% in 2025. For example, county governments committed KES 130 million in coinvestments, signalling big interest, engagement and commitment.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
